purpose: Core collector registry: consistent snapshots, whole-set provisioning updates.
overview: registry.go holds the authoritative collector membership, hands out name-ordered snapshots for stable row alignment, and applies provisioning updates as epoch-bumped whole-set replacements.
language: go

--- source: "internal/core/registry.go" (lines 1-46, similarity: 1.00) ---
1| package core
2| 
3| import (
4| 	"sort"
5| 	"sync"
6| )
7| 
8| // registry is the authoritative set of core collectors. Membership
9| // changes arrive from the provisioning pipeline and take effect on
10| // the next probe round; the registry never mutates mid-round, so a
11| // round sees one consistent snapshot.
12| type registry struct {
13| 	mu      sync.RWMutex
14| 	entries map[string]collectorEntry
15| 	epoch   uint64
16| }
17| 
18| // snapshot returns the current membership in stable name order. The
19| // sort is deliberate: probe rounds, reports, and the fleet dashboard
20| // all walk the same order, which keeps their row alignment stable
21| // across refreshes.
22| func (r *registry) snapshot() []collectorEntry {
23| 	r.mu.RLock()
24| 	defer r.mu.RUnlock()
25| 	out := make([]collectorEntry, 0, len(r.entries))
26| 	for _, e := range r.entries {
27| 		out = append(out, e)
28| 	}
29| 	sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].name < out[j].name })
30| 	return out
31| }
32| 
33| // apply installs a provisioning update and bumps the epoch. Updates
34| // are whole-set replacements: partial merges once produced ghosts
35| // when a rename raced a removal, and the epoch lets probe rounds
36| // detect that membership moved under them.
37| func (r *registry) apply(update []collectorEntry) {
38| 	r.mu.Lock()
39| 	defer r.mu.Unlock()
40| 	next := make(map[string]collectorEntry, len(update))
41| 	for _, e := range update {
42| 		next[e.name] = e
43| 	}
44| 	r.entries = next
45| 	r.epoch++
46| }
